goal: After every deploy the CI job itself requests Kaizena Flow's home and one template-store page, logs status, bytes and cache headers, and fails on anything but 200; and Kaizena Flow's own store is prerendered with each build while its site is served from it.
why: Today scripts/await-deploy.mjs checks /api/health and 2 API routes and 0 pages, so the first visitor after each deploy pays the cold draw and a page that cannot load is found by a person. After: 2 pages are checked on every deploy, and kaizenaflow.com's markets are built with the deploy.

commits.title: The deploy job requests two pages after production runs the commit

changes.how: Add three exports beside SMOKE_CHECKS and smokeProblems. (1) `export function smokePages(value)`: takes the SMOKE_PAGES variable (a string of addresses separated by commas; each a path starting with '/' or a full https:// address), trims each, drops empty ones, and returns the list; when value is empty or undefined it returns ['/', '/s/demo/no']. (2) `export function pageProblems(results)`: results are { address, status, bytes, cache } objects; it returns one line per result whose status is not 200, in the form `GET <address>: <status or 'no answer'> (expected 200)`; empty when all are 200. (3) `export function pageLine(result)`: returns `GET <address>: <status>, <bytes> bytes, x-vercel-cache <value or 'none'>, x-nextjs-cache <value or 'none'>`. Add `async function pageResults(url, pages)`: for each page, one after the other (not Promise.all, so the first request starts the proxy and the page function alone), fetch it with method GET, redirect: 'follow', headers { 'User-Agent': 'kaizena-flow-deploy-check' }, signal AbortSignal.timeout(30_000); a path is requested as `${url}${path}`, a full address as it is; read the body with await response.arrayBuffer() for the byte count; return { address, status, bytes, cache: { vercel: response.headers.get('x-vercel-cache'), next: response.headers.get('x-nextjs-cache') } }; on a throw return { address, status: null, bytes: 0, cache: { vercel: null, next: null } }. In main(), after the line that prints 'Each route for outsiders refuses a call without a token' and before its `return`, add: read `const pages = smokePages(process.env.SMOKE_PAGES)`; get results; if pageProblems(results) is not empty, wait 60 seconds and get them once more (the same retry the route checks use); print pageLine() for every result with console.log; if problems remain, console.error(`Production runs the commit, but a page does not answer 200:\n${problems.join('\n')}`) and process.exit(1). Then request each page a second time and print its pageLine() again under the words 'Second request:' (this is the line that shows the cache header of a prerendered page: HIT or PRERENDER). Extend the file's top comment: add the SMOKE_PAGES variable to the list of variables and one sentence saying the job, not a visitor, pays the first draw of these pages. Keep SMOKE_CHECKS, deployVerdict and the waiting loop exactly as they are.

Import pageLine, pageProblems and smokePages too. Add a describe('page checks') with these cases: smokePages(undefined) and smokePages('') equal ['/', '/s/demo/no']; smokePages(' /, /s/demo/no ,https://example.com/x ,') equals ['/', '/s/demo/no', 'https://example.com/x']; pageProblems of two results with status 200 is []; pageProblems([{ address: '/', status: 500, bytes: 0, cache: { vercel: null, next: null } }, { address: '/s/demo/no', status: null, bytes: 0, cache: { vercel: null, next: null } }]) equals ['GET /: 500 (expected 200)', 'GET /s/demo/no: no answer (expected 200)']; pageLine({ address: '/', status: 200, bytes: 48213, cache: { vercel: 'HIT', next: null } }) equals 'GET /: 200, 48213 bytes, x-vercel-cache HIT, x-nextjs-cache none'. Change no existing case.

There are three steps named 'Wait until production runs this commit' (they run `node scripts/await-deploy.mjs`, near lines 326, 392 and 414). In the env block of each, directly under the PRODUCTION_URL line, add: `SMOKE_PAGES: ${{ vars.SMOKE_PAGES || '/,/s/demo/no' }}` with the same indentation. Change nothing else in the workflow.

In the paragraph that begins 'Either way the job then waits for production to run the commit (D389, `scripts/await-deploy.mjs`)', add after its last sentence: 'It then requests the pages of `SMOKE_PAGES` (a repository variable; by default Kaizena Flow's home and the template store's Norwegian front page), one after the other and each twice: the job, not a visitor, pays the first cold draw, the log shows each page's status, bytes and cache headers, and a page that does not answer 200 fails the job (bloat review step 0.3).'

In the Workflow section, in the bullet 'Production is deployed by CI', change the last sentence 'Each deploy then waits until `/api/health` reports the commit (D389, `scripts/await-deploy.mjs`), and fails the job when it does not.' to 'Each deploy then waits until `/api/health` reports the commit (D389, `scripts/await-deploy.mjs`), then requests two pages (`SMOKE_PAGES`), and fails the job when the commit does not arrive or a page does not answer 200.' Change no other line.
